anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description: Definition: Root cause located in the transaction-log subsystem, where the generation, flushing, switching, archiving, or retention of write-ahead log records becomes the bottleneck on the write path. It is distinct from generic storage I/O because the bottleneck is specific to the log-file group, log buffer, archiver process, and replication-retention pipeline rather than to overall device capacity. Observable phenomena: rising commit latency, elevated log-flush, log-write, and log-sync wait events, frequent log-file switches and checkpoint storms reported in engine alert logs, continuously growing log-file and archive directories, archival processes lagging behind the latest log position, and write workloads stalling when the next log segment is unavailable. Possible contributing factors: log files undersized relative to the peak redo generation rate, too few log groups or log segments, log files placed on the same device as busy data or temporary files, log buffer and commit-batching parameters not tuned for the workload, archive destinations slow or full, replication-state objects retaining log segments because downstream consumers are disconnected, and synchronous-commit policies enabled without validating the latency budget.

entry.official_definition: Maximum wait for connection, in seconds; zero or not specified means wait indefinitely.
entry.trigger_condition: A libpq client connection attempt exceeds connect_timeout seconds.
entry.workload_impact: The client connection attempt fails instead of waiting indefinitely.
entry.default_behavior: Zero or absent value means wait indefinitely.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
